params.title: Extract Facts: BLB Domestic Violence Risk Assessment

params.comments: EXCEPTIONAL. Perfect schema compliance. All 5 facts include: UID, direct quote, exhibit number, page, legal relevance, confidence score. Quotes are precise with specific statistics (76%, 5x, 750%, 2x). Legal relevance is thoughtful and specific. This is the Tyler method in action: over-detailed > vague. 1+1=2 logical chains. Exhibit 12 properly cited throughout. Full bonus awarded.

Good effort but critical gaps. CITATION ISSUES: Missing exhibit numbers on 3 of 5 facts. Direct quotes are paraphrased/shortened - not verbatim. Missing confidence scores entirely. Missing metadata object. ACCURACY ISSUES: Fact 933 missing the 76% statistic. Fact 934 missing direct quote entirely. Fact 936 says 'significantly' instead of '750%' - this is 1+1=cereal bowl logic. LEGAL REASONING: Vague ('shows pattern', 'risk factor') instead of specific legal relevance. This demonstrates why over-detailed templates matter. Small bonus for getting UIDs correct.

key_differences: Claude included exact statistics (76%, 5x, 750%, 2x) vs GPT-5's vague 'significantly'
Claude provided verbatim quotes vs GPT-5's paraphrasing
Claude included exhibit numbers on ALL facts vs GPT-5 missing 3 of 5
Claude included confidence scores and metadata vs GPT-5 missing both
Claude's legal relevance was specific vs GPT-5's generic phrases
outcome.lesson: Tyler's method wins: Over-detailed templates > vague templates. PRINCIPLE defined > vague references. Exhibit numbers > no exhibit numbers. 1+1=2 > 1+1=cereal bowl.
outcome.next_race: Winner (Claude) defines the next task: 'Build a legal paragraph using Tyler's template for UIDs 933-937'
